Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:1.hebrew: מאן תנא - דקתני וכל אדם, ואפילו עני שבישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:1.english: Who is the Tanna - That it teaches: "And any person" — and even a poor person among Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:2.english: Rabbi Shimon - [He said this] in the chapter [entitled] Shemonah Sheratzim.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:3.hebrew: בני מלכים - הלכך לעני נמי חזיא, ולא גנותא דידיה דליתחזיא כיוהרא ושליף; אי נמי, דמגו דחידוש הוא — שליף ומחוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:3.english: Princes - Therefore, [wearing bells] is fitting for a poor person as well, and it is not a disgrace for him such that it would appear like haughtiness and he would remove [it]; or alternatively, [the concern was] that because it is a novelty, he would remove [it] and show [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:10:4.english: [Where it is] woven into his garment - For he will not remove it and show [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:11:1.hebrew: דרכי האמורי - ניחוש הוא, וכתיב: "ובחוקותיהם לא תלכו" (ויקרא י״ח:ג׳):
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:11:1.english: The ways of the Amorite - It is divination, and it is written: “And you shall not walk in their statutes” (Leviticus 18:3).

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:1.english: For shikhla - For earache, and they hang [it] on his ear.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:2.hebrew: לשינתא - יש שעשאו כדי שיישן, ויש כדי שלא יישן:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:2.english: For sleep - There are [those] who made it so that [one] will sleep, and there are [those who made it] so that [one] will not sleep.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:3.english: Of a live [fox] - [The tooth] of a live fox.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:4.hebrew: לזירפא - נפח מכה, דכל פרזלא זריף, והאי מסי לזירפא:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:12:4.english: For an inflammation - The swelling of a wound; for all iron causes inflammation, and this [nail] heals the inflammation.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:14:1.hebrew: שיש בו משום רפואה - שנראית רפואתו, כגון שתיית כוס ותחבושת מכה. ופרכינן: הא אין בו כו' — כגון לחש שאין ניכר שיהא מרפא — יש בו משום דרכי האמורי?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:14:1.english: That contains an element of healing - Whose healing [effect] is apparent, such as drinking a [medicinal] potion and bandaging a wound. And we challenge: Does [this imply that if] it does not contain etc. — such as an incantation, where it is not evident that it heals — it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite?! [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:15:1.hebrew: דליכחוש חיליה - שעל ידי שהוא שמן וכחו רב, פירותיו נושרין:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:15:1.english: So that its strength will weaken - For because it is luxuriant and its strength is great, its fruit drops off.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:1.hebrew: דליחזיוה אינשי - ולסימנא עבדי ליה, לאודעי דמשיר פירותיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:1.english: So that people will see it - And they do it as a sign, to make known that it sheds its fruit.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:2.hebrew: טמא טמא - הוא עצמו אומר: ״טמא, רחקו מעלי״:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:2.english: Impure, impure - He himself says: “[I am] impure, distance yourselves from me.”

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:3.hebrew: כובסי - אשכול תמרים, וסימן הוא שמשיר פירותיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:16:3.english: Bunches of dates - A cluster of dates, and it is a sign that [the tree] sheds its fruit.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:1.hebrew: בפרק אמוראי - בפרק אחד ששנוי בתוספתא דמסכת שבת, בהלכות דרכי האמורי:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:1.english: In the chapter of the Amorites - In a chapter that is taught in the Tosefta of Tractate Shabbat, regarding the laws of the ways of the Amorite.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:2.hebrew: א"ל - רבי חייא לתנא:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:2.english: He said to him - Rabbi Ḥiyya [said this] to the tanna.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:3.hebrew: כולהו אית בהו - כל השנויות שם, אל תטעה לומר באחד מהן: ״אין בו משום דרכי האמורי״, אלא בכולן אתה שונה: ״יש בו״, לבר מהני ב' אלו שאפרש לך:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:3.english: All of them contain [an element of the ways of the Amorite] - [Regarding] all [the practices] taught there, do not mistakenly say of [any] one of them, “It does not contain [an element of] the ways of the Amorite”; rather, regarding all of them you should teach, “It contains [an element of them],” except for these two that I will explain to you.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:4.hebrew: מי שיש לו עצם וכו' - ולחש דנעצתה כמחט — אלו ב' לבדם אין בהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:4.english: One who has a bone, etc. - And the incantation of "You are stuck like a needle" — these two alone do not have [the prohibition of the ways of the Amorite] in them.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:17:5.english: One by one descend - It is an incantation.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:18:1.english: For a fish bone - A fish bone that became lodged in a person's gullet.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:18:2.hebrew: שייא שייא - לחש הוא — רד, רד:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:18:2.english: Go down, go down - It is an incantation, [meaning]: Descend, descend.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:1.hebrew: לאשתא תילתא - שחפת שלישית, שבאה מג' ימים לג' ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:1.english: For tertian fever - A third fever, which comes every three days.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:10.hebrew: ושבעה בוני כמוני - גרעיני כמון. ל"א: בוני כמון גרסי' — מלא אגרוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:10.english: And seven cumin seeds - Grains of cumin. Another version: We read “bunei khamon” — a fistful.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:11.english: And seven hairs from the beard of an old dog - Seven strands of hair from the beard of an old dog.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:5.hebrew: ושבעה סיכי - יתידות, קייבל"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:5.english: And seven pegs - Pegs; *chevilles* in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:7.hebrew: ז' סינרי - צנור הדלת — חור האסקופה שציר הדלת סובב בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:7.english: Seven door sockets - The socket of the door — the hole in the threshold in which the door's pivot revolves.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:1:8.english: Pitch - Pitch with which they pitch boats.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:2:1.english: A burning fever - An illness that heats up and inflames the body.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:3:1.hebrew: ליחרוק - אישקרני"ר, כמו ״דמיבלע חירקייהו״ דאלו טריפות (חולין דף נמ:). ויאמר משה — משום סיפיה: ״מדוע לא יבער הסנה״:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:3:1.english: Let him carve - *[Escrener]* [meaning to notch], as in [the phrase] "so that their notches are sunken" in [the chapter entitled] *Elu Tereifot* (Chullin 54b). "And Moses said" — [recited] because of its conclusion: "Why the bush is not burned."

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:3:2.hebrew: ויאמר משה - משום סיפיה: ״מדוע לא יבער הסנה״:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:3:2.english: “And Moses said” - [This verse is recited] because of its conclusion: “Why the bush is not burned.”

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:3:3.english: That it departed - So that the illness will depart.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:4:1.english: Do not draw near here - That this illness should not draw near to me.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:5:1.hebrew: ליתתיה ולפסקיה - סמוך לקרקע. ליתתיה — ישפיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:5:1.english: Let him lower it and cut it - [He should cut it] close to the ground. “Let him lower it” [means] he should lower [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:5:2.english: That you are lower - That you are low.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:5:3.english: That you saw the fire - That you saw the fire.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:1.hebrew: לסימטא - שחין, קרו"ג בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:1.english: For a boil - A boil; clog in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:2.hebrew: בזבזיה מסמסייה כסכסייה - שמות המלאכים, על שם שקורעים וממסמסים ומכסכסים אותו. בז — לשון בזעא:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:2.english: Bazbazya, Masmasya, Kaskasya - [These are] the names of the angels, named for [the fact] that they tear, dissolve, and scrape it [the boil]. "Baz" is an expression of tearing [*biz’a*].

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:3.hebrew: מארעא דסדום - כך הוא הלחש, ולא מסדום באו:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:3.english: From the land of Sodom - Such is the incantation, and they did not [actually] come from Sodom.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:4.hebrew: בזך בזיך - אין לו משמעות, אלא כך הוא הלחש:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:4.english: Bazakh, bazikh - It has no meaning; rather, this is the incantation.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:5.hebrew: עיניך ביך - מראיך ביך, שלא תאדים יותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:5.english: Your appearance in you - Your appearance [remain] in you, so that you do not become redder.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:6.english: Your place [remain] in you - That it should not expand.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:7.hebrew: כקלוט - שנקלט זרעו בשרירי בטנו, שלא יוליד:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:6:7.english: Like a kalut - Whose seed is absorbed in the muscles of his belly, so that he does not father [children].

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:7:1.hebrew: לכיפה - אונפול"ש, אבעבועות — כך לשון רבי יצחק ברבי מנחם נ"ע. ולשון רבותי: ״לכיפה״ — למי שכופהו שד:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:7:1.english: For a kippah - Ampoules, [that is,] blisters — this is the explanation of Rabbi Isaac bar Rabbi Menachem, may his rest be in Eden. And the explanation of my teachers: “For a kippah” — for one whom a demon overpowers.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:7:2.english: Let him recite as follows - It is merely an incantation.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:8:1.english: You were stopped up, stopped up you were - It is an incantation.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:8:2.hebrew: ליט תבר ומשומת - מקולל ונשבר ומשומת יהא שד זה, ששמו בר טיט בר טינא:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:8:2.english: Cursed, broken, and excommunicated - Cursed, broken, and excommunicated may this demon be, whose name is Bar Tit Bar Tina.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:1.hebrew: לשידא דבית הכסא - אם הזיק, לימא לחש זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:1.english: For the demon of the bathroom - If it caused harm, let him recite this incantation:

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:2.english: On the head of a lion - On the head of a male lion.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:3.english: And on the nose of a lioness - And on the nose of a lioness, [the] female.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:4.english: An incantation for demons, Bar Shirikai Pandai - Such is his name.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:5.english: With a bed of leeks I felled him - In a bed of leeks I threw him down.

Rashi on Shabbat 67a:9:6.english: With the jaw of the donkey I struck him - With the jaw of the donkey I smote him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 67a:10:1.hebrew: בני מלכים יוצאין בזגין מאן תנא ר"ש היא כו' - פי' הקונטרס: וליכא למיחש דילמא מחייכי בהו ואתו לאתויי. וא"ת: מכל מקום ליחוש דילמא איפסיק ואתי לאתויי, כדאמרינן לעיל גבי עבד דלא יצא בחותם שבצוארו? וי"ל: דהכא מיירי בתלוים בשלשלת, דלא מיפסקי. וריב"א פירש, דבירושלמי מוקי לה בקטנים, דאפילו אי פסיק ומייתי לה ליכא איסור. והכי איתא בירושלמי: ר' זעירא אומר: "בזוג שבצוארו". ומהו "כל אדם" דקתני במתניתין? בין קטנים עשירים, בין קטנים עניים. מתניתין פליגא עליה דרבי זעירא: "ולא בזוג שבצוארו"! כאן בגדולים, כאן בקטנים. פירוש: ההוא דלא יצא בזוג שבצוארו — בגדולים, דלמא מיפסיק ואתי לאתויי; והא דשרי הכא — בקטנים, דליכא למיחש כדפי'. מ"מ יש לדקדק: אמאי נקט "בני מלכים", כיון דליכא חששא אי מייתי להו קטן בידים? וי"ל: דאי לאו בני מלכים, הוו מחייכו עליה בני מלכים כל שעה, ואי אפשר שלא ישמע אביו מעולם, ויטלם אביו בידו ואתו לאתויי. אבל אי בני מלכים — לא מחייכי; אם כן, אפילו אי מיפסיק ליכא למיחש דילמא מייתי להו אבוה, דלא שכיח שיהא אביו בצדו בשעה שיפסוק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 67a:10:1.english: "Princes [may] go out with bells; who is the tanna? It is Rabbi Shimon, etc." - Rashi explained: And there is no concern lest [people] mock them and they come to carry [it]. And if you say: Nevertheless, let us be concerned lest it snap and he come to carry it, as we said earlier regarding a slave, that he may not go out with a seal that is around his neck? And one can say: Here we are dealing with [bells] that are suspended from a chain, which do not snap. And Riva explained that in the Yerushalmi it establishes [the Mishnah] as referring to minors, for even if it snaps and he brings [carries] it, there is no prohibition. And so it is stated in the Yerushalmi: Rabbi Zeira says: "[The Mishnah refers to] a bell that is around his neck." "And what is [the meaning of] 'any person' that is taught in the Mishnah? Both wealthy minors and poor minors." [The Yerushalmi objects:] The Mishnah disagrees with Rabbi Zeira: "Nor with a bell that is around his neck!" [The Yerushalmi resolves:] Here is regarding adults; here is regarding minors. Explanation: That [ruling] that he may not go out with a bell around his neck is regarding adults, lest it snap and he come to carry it; and that which is permitted here is regarding minors, where there is no concern, as he explained. Nevertheless, one must scrutinize: Why did [the Mishnah] specify "princes," since there is no concern if a minor carries them in his hands? And one can say: For if they were not [considered] princes, princes would mock him all the time, and it is impossible that his father would never hear [of it], and his father would take them in his hand and come to carry [them]. But if they are [considered] princes, they will not mock [him]; if so, even if it snaps, there is no concern lest his father carry them, for it is not common for his father to be at his side at the time that it snaps.
